title: Adani Ports to buy Dutch fuel-storage firm Evos for €2.56 billion
dek: The all-cash, debt-funded deal adds eight terminals in five European countries and takes Adani Ports to 28 ports and terminals in 10 countries.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ) has agreed to buy Evos, a Dutch company that runs fuel and chemical storage terminals at eight European ports, in an all-cash deal that values the business at €2.56 billion (about $2.88 billion) including debt. It is the Indian port operator's biggest step yet into Europe.

APSEZ will buy all of Evos B.V. from Igneo Infrastructure Partners, the company said in a statement on Thursday evening. The equity value, what it pays for the shares after taking on Evos's debt, is €1.18 billion. The deal will be funded with debt: the Japanese bank MUFG is the sole underwriter and has committed financing of up to €2.8 billion. It still needs regulatory and other approvals and a consultation with Evos's works council, a staff body that European law requires to be consulted.

## What APSEZ is buying

APSEZ describes Evos as Europe's second-largest independent liquid storage operator. According to the company's statement, it has:

- eight port-based terminals in the Netherlands, Germany, Spain, Belgium and Malta
- 6.3 million cubic metres of storage in 452 tanks, and 63 berths for ships and barges
- pipeline links that include Amsterdam's Schiphol airport and the Central Europe Pipeline System
- 37 million tonnes of cargo handled in 2025, and average occupancy of 99%
- revenue of €392 million and EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) of €219 million in 2025, a margin of 56%

The terminals store petrol, diesel, marine fuel and jet fuel as well as newer fuels such as sustainable aviation fuel, biofuels, methanol and bioethanol. Most revenue comes from "take-or-pay" contracts, under which customers pay for storage space whether they use it or not, and many contracts are linked to inflation, the company said.

The price is 11.7 times Evos's 2025 EBITDA. Analysts at JM Financial put it at 11.4 times their 2026 estimate, compared with 10.2 times for Royal Vopak, the listed Dutch storage company, Business Today reported.

## What the company says

"Evos marks an important milestone in APSEZ's trajectory towards handling 1 billion tons of cargo," Managing Director Karan Adani said in the statement. The company said the deal would take it to 28 ports and terminals in 10 countries, add a sizeable presence in Europe and broaden its liquids business, which is smaller than its container and bulk operations.

APSEZ said its net debt would rise to 2.76 times EBITDA on a combined basis, using its own figures for the last financial year and Evos's for 2025, and that it expected this to fall to about 2.5 times by March 2027. It had cash of Rs 12,502 crore at the end of September. Its international ports, which include terminals in Sri Lanka, Tanzania and Australia, earned an EBITDA margin of 44.8% in April-September, below Evos's.

## How the market took it

Adani Ports shares fell 1.3% on Thursday to close at Rs 1,884.6, Reuters reported, as the deal was announced. On Friday they recovered, rising as much as 2.1% to an intraday high of Rs 1,937.40, close to the record of Rs 1,949.05 touched in the previous session, Business Today reported.

Brokers were mostly positive. JM Financial called the deal "largely neutral" at first and kept a buy rating with a target of Rs 2,065. Motilal Oswal kept a buy rating with a target of Rs 2,170, and Elara Capital raised its target to Rs 2,432 from Rs 2,107, according to Business Today. JM Financial expects the deal to close within 15 months.

## Background

Adani Ports, India's largest private port operator, has been expanding abroad: it runs the Colombo West International Terminal in Sri Lanka, terminals in Tanzania, and the North Queensland Export Terminal in Australia, and it operates the Haldia terminal in Bengal. The company's interest in Evos was reported late last month, when NewsBytes said it had made a binding offer; that followed an unsuccessful attempt to buy Associated British Ports in the UK, according to the same report.

## What happens next

APSEZ said the approval processes and the works council consultation would begin straight away. It did not give a closing date.
